The terms that suit a network

Source: R/specify_terms.R, R/report_specify.R
specify_terms.Rd

Without a formula, or with . as its whole right-hand side, as in advice ~ ., specify_mrqap() and specify_ergm() return a table of every term that the model can take for .data, as RSiena::getEffects() does for a Siena data object. Each term is written out for the network's layers and node attributes, such as ego(age), same(dept), tie(friends), and indeg(friends, node = 'ego'). Choose rows with [ or dplyr::filter(), and formula() of the rows gives the formula of those terms. terms_mrqap says what each term measures.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'specify_terms'
formula(x, lhs = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specify_terms'
tidy(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The table of every term.

lhs

The outcome of the formula, as a name or a string. NULL, the default, is the outcome the table was made for.

...

Not used.

Value

The table is a tibble of class "mrqap_terms" or "ergm_terms", and also "specify_terms", with the columns term, effect, layer, and attribute. print() shows every row, and tidy() returns the table as a plain tibble. formula() returns the formula of the chosen rows, as specify_mrqap() or specify_ergm() returns it.

Which terms are listed

  • A numeric attribute gets ego(), alter(), diff(), and sim(), and a categorical one ego(), alter(), same(), and mix(). A name, a label, or an attribute with a different category for each node gets no term.

  • An undirected network has no alter(), exchange(), outdeg(), or recip, since the two sides of its ties are the same.

  • A two-mode network reads ego() on the first mode and alter() on the second. A term of both sides needs the attribute on both modes.

  • The reporter terms are only for a cognitive social structure, and global() only for a list of networks. An MRQAP takes inertia and trans only on a panel.

  • A term that the model drops or refuses, such as tie() of the outcome layer, has no row. Nor has a term that reads the outcome's own ties, such as recip in an MRQAP of one network, since permuting the outcome does not permute the term with it.

The terms are for the outcome on the left-hand side, by default .. Where . is not one layer, as in a multiplex network without a focal layer, the terms are for its first layer, and a message says so.

A formula of chosen rows

formula() of the rows gives the formula of their terms, read by the same specify_*() function, for the same outcome or for lhs. What the model makes of each term is in the record of that formula, as specify describes. Some terms measure the same thing in different ways: same(x), same(x, diff = TRUE), and mix(x), and diff(x) and sim(x). Of each such set, formula() keeps the first row, and a message names the others, since a model of all of them is collinear. For the formula that a regression fitted, see netreg_results.

See also

terms_mrqap for what each term measures, and specify for what each model makes of a formula.

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

# Every term for a network, and a formula of some of them
terms <- specify_mrqap(advice ~ ., ison_hightech)
terms
#> 52 terms for an MRQAP of advice
#> # A tibble: 52 × 4
#>    term                                    effect         layer   attribute
#>    <chr>                                   <chr>          <chr>   <chr>    
#>  1 ego(age)                                ego            NA      age      
#>  2 alter(age)                              alter          NA      age      
#>  3 diff(age)                               diff           NA      age      
#>  4 diff(age, transformer_fn = identity)    diff           NA      age      
#>  5 sim(age)                                sim            NA      age      
#>  6 ego(tenure)                             ego            NA      tenure   
#>  7 alter(tenure)                           alter          NA      tenure   
#>  8 diff(tenure)                            diff           NA      tenure   
#>  9 diff(tenure, transformer_fn = identity) diff           NA      tenure   
#> 10 sim(tenure)                             sim            NA      tenure   
#> 11 ego(level)                              ego            NA      level    
#> 12 alter(level)                            alter          NA      level    
#> 13 diff(level)                             diff           NA      level    
#> 14 diff(level, transformer_fn = identity)  diff           NA      level    
#> 15 sim(level)                              sim            NA      level    
#> 16 ego(dept)                               ego            NA      dept     
#> 17 alter(dept)                             alter          NA      dept     
#> 18 same(dept)                              same           NA      dept     
#> 19 same(dept, diff = TRUE)                 same           NA      dept     
#> 20 mix(dept)                               mix            NA      dept     
#> 21 tie(friends)                            tie            friends NA       
#> 22 exchange(friends)                       exchange       friends NA       
#> 23 indeg(friends)                          indeg          friends NA       
#> 24 indeg(friends, node = 'ego')            indeg          friends NA       
#> 25 outdeg(friends)                         outdeg         friends NA       
#> 26 outdeg(friends, node = 'alter')         outdeg         friends NA       
#> 27 tertius(friends, age)                   tertius        friends age      
#> 28 tertius_diff(friends, age)              tertius_diff   friends age      
#> 29 tertius(friends, tenure)                tertius        friends tenure   
#> 30 tertius_diff(friends, tenure)           tertius_diff   friends tenure   
#> 31 tertius(friends, level)                 tertius        friends level    
#> 32 tertius_diff(friends, level)            tertius_diff   friends level    
#> 33 tie(reports)                            tie            reports NA       
#> 34 exchange(reports)                       exchange       reports NA       
#> 35 indeg(reports)                          indeg          reports NA       
#> 36 indeg(reports, node = 'ego')            indeg          reports NA       
#> 37 outdeg(reports)                         outdeg         reports NA       
#> 38 outdeg(reports, node = 'alter')         outdeg         reports NA       
#> 39 tertius(reports, age)                   tertius        reports age      
#> 40 tertius_diff(reports, age)              tertius_diff   reports age      
#> 41 tertius(reports, tenure)                tertius        reports tenure   
#> 42 tertius_diff(reports, tenure)           tertius_diff   reports tenure   
#> 43 tertius(reports, level)                 tertius        reports level    
#> 44 tertius_diff(reports, level)            tertius_diff   reports level    
#> 45 reporter(age)                           reporter       NA      age      
#> 46 reporter(tenure)                        reporter       NA      tenure   
#> 47 reporter(level)                         reporter       NA      level    
#> 48 reporter(dept)                          reporter       NA      dept     
#> 49 reporter_ego                            reporter_ego   NA      NA       
#> 50 reporter_alter                          reporter_alter NA      NA       
#> 51 reporter_same(dept)                     reporter_same  NA      dept     
#> 52 reporter_same(dept, node = 'alter')     reporter_same  NA      dept     
#> Choose rows, and `formula()` of them gives their formula.
formula(terms[terms$term %in% c("ego(age)", "same(dept)", "tie(friends)"), ])
#> # An MRQAP formula
#> 
#> advice ~ ego(age) + same(dept) + tie(friends)
formula(terms[terms$effect == "reporter", ], friends)
#> # An MRQAP formula
#> 
#> friends ~ reporter(age) + reporter(tenure) + reporter(level) + 
#>     reporter(dept)
